brief: How to keep going once the work stops being exciting

slots.subtitle: Six ways to keep working through the part where nothing feels like progress, none of which involve motivation.
slots.item1: Why the middle is where most work is abandoned
slots.item2: The smallest unit that still counts as done
slots.coverNote: Discipline is a system, not a personality

slots.body: Not because small tasks matter, but because beginning is the expensive part and a step you cannot talk yourself out of removes the negotiation entirely.
slots.p1Body: Set the bar low enough that a bad day still clears it.
slots.p2Body: A decision you make once beats one you make every morning.
slots.pullLine: The bar is not what you can do on a good day. It is what you will still clear on a bad one.

slots.body: Stopping at a natural end means tomorrow begins with a blank page. Stopping mid-sentence means it begins with an obvious next move, which is a much cheaper start.
slots.p1Body: The urge to finish the section is what costs you the next session.
slots.p2Body: One sentence about what comes next, for the version of you who forgot.
slots.pullLine: Tomorrow you will not remember what you meant. Leave the sentence unfinished and it will not matter.

slots.body: Output varies for reasons you do not control. Showing up does not, which makes it the only honest thing to track and the only one that survives a bad week.
slots.p1Body: Nothing more elaborate. Elaborate systems are avoidance.
slots.p2Body: One missed day is noise. Two is the beginning of a different habit.
slots.pullLine: Output is weather. Showing up is climate.

slots.body: Most people give their sharpest two hours to correspondence and attempt the difficult work on what is left. The order is the whole problem, and it is free to change.
slots.p1Body: Before the inbox, before anybody else has made a claim on the day.
slots.p2Body: A reply at four in the afternoon is indistinguishable from one at nine.
slots.pullLine: Nobody protects the morning, and then wonders where the year went.

slots.body: It arrives at roughly the same point in everything, which is a fact about the shape of projects rather than about this one. It is information about the middle, not about the work.
slots.p1Body: Naming it in advance removes most of its authority.
slots.p2Title: Change the task, not the project
slots.p2Body: Move to a different part of the same thing before abandoning it.
slots.pullLine: The middle of a project feels identical to the end of your interest in it. It is not the same thing.

slots.body: Persistence applied to the wrong thing is just an expensive way to be wrong for longer. The test is not whether it is hard — it is whether it still matters to you when it is.
slots.p1Body: On a good day, not on the worst one, when the answer is unreliable.
slots.p2Body: An abandoned project left open costs attention every week forever.
slots.pullLine: Quitting badly costs a year. Quitting deliberately costs an afternoon.

slots.body: Not an hour, not a plan, not a new system. Ten minutes on the thing you have been avoiding, at the same time, tomorrow.
slots.closingLine: Consistency is not a feeling you wait for. It is a decision you only have to make once.
slots.signoff: The middle is where everything gets abandoned
